turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt900_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (O, Sb, Co, Si, Sn, Ca, Ni, Ti, Pb, Se, Ge, Cu, Zr, Te, S, Zn,
    Fe, Yb, Mn, Sr, Nb, Bi, Cd, Hf, In) and `target` (the measured zT
    (thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K).
  - b3_te_zt900_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 900 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 900 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set is sorted by increasing \(zT\) and is dominated at the high end by a small number of well-known thermoelectric families. The extreme values (\(zT>2\)) belong exclusively to Pb-chalcogenide alloys (PbTe–PbS, PbTe–PbSe, Sr-doped PbTe). The next tier (\(zT\approx1.3{-}1.7\)) consists of off-stoichiometry \(\mathrm{Cu_2Se}\) and a few half-Heusler compositions (\((\mathrm{Zr,Hf})\mathrm{NiSn}\) and \(\mathrm{ZrCoBi}\)-type). All other chemistries (oxides, SiGe, HMS, undoped 1:1 PbTe/PbSe, FeNbSb, Zintls, etc.) remain \(\lesssim1.1\).

Direct composition matching of the 100-member pool against these high-\(zT\) exemplars yields a clear ranking:

- c052 (\(\mathrm{Pb}_{0.49}\mathrm{Te}_{0.39}\mathrm{S}_{0.10}\)) is the only pool member that lies inside the PbTe–PbS solid-solution field that produced the two highest training points (\(zT=2.21\) and \(1.28\)).
- c054 and c063 are stoichiometric \(\mathrm{Cu_2Se}\) and sit nearest the training points that reached \(zT=1.74\) and \(1.45\).
- c078 is essentially \((\mathrm{Zr}_{0.4}\mathrm{Hf}_{0.6})\mathrm{NiSn}\), reproducing the half-Heusler compositions that reached \(zT=1.32{-}1.35\).
- c086 reproduces the \(\mathrm{ZrCo}(\mathrm{Bi,Sn})\) half-Heusler that reached \(zT=1.33\).

No other pool entry is compositionally closer to any training sample with \(zT>1.2\). Consequently the five candidates expected to give the highest \(zT(900\,\mathrm{K})\) are, in decreasing order:

Final: c052, c054, c063, c078, c086
